scenarioSubtitle: Designing an AI-enabled SME customer journey
description: Participants make AI leadership decisions across seven stages of the SME customer journey. Each decision shapes customer experience, trust, adoption, and economic value — revealing how AI strategy creates or destroys ROI over time.

rounds.title: How should AI shape SME acquisition — and at what cost?
rounds.prompt: The bank wants to use AI to improve how it targets and reaches SME prospects. The AI analyses signals such as sector, growth stage, transaction patterns, and digital behaviour to identify strong leads and personalise outreach. The key decision is where to focus the AI's effort: apply it across all prospects, concentrate it on the most promising customers, or keep the existing campaign system.

options.label: Use AI to personalise outreach for every SME prospect — apply the same level of AI effort across all leads, regardless of how likely they are to convert.
options.insightExperience: Applying AI to every prospect, regardless of conversion likelihood, generates volume without precision. The AI cannot distinguish strong leads from weak ones, so the customers acquired are less well-matched and less likely to stay engaged.
options.insightCostDrivers: The £1.2M cost comes from running AI across the entire prospect pool — the most expensive acquisition approach, and the least efficient in terms of revenue generated per pound spent.
options.insightRevenue: Customers acquired this way are less engaged from the start. Activation rates are lower, CVI grows more slowly, and the revenue gap versus the optimal path compounds through every subsequent stage.

compareSummary.reason: Spends £300K more than Option A but without the targeting focus that drives conversion — running AI across all prospects rather than the strongest ones produces lower conversion rates and a weaker starting customer base.

options.explanation: By applying AI equally to every prospect, the system generates personalised outreach but cannot distinguish a strong lead from a weak one. The £1.2M cost comes from running AI at full scale across the entire prospect pool. Without any targeting focus, conversion rates are diluted and the customers acquired are less well-matched to what the bank offers. This shows up in the CVI chart: an early uplift that fades faster than the optimal path as poorly matched customers disengage through Activation and Engagement. Compared to Option A, the lack of targeting precision means weaker customers, lower adoption, and cumulative revenue £800K short of the optimal outcome.

options.label: Focus AI personalisation on the highest-potential prospects — apply full AI effort where conversion signals are strongest, and use simple templates for the rest.
options.insightExperience: By focusing AI effort on prospects where conversion signals are strongest — sector data, growth stage, digital behaviour — the AI works with precision. The customers acquired this way are better matched, more engaged, and more likely to activate fully.
options.insightCostDrivers: The £900K cost covers targeted AI on the strongest prospects plus a lighter classification layer for the rest — the best revenue return per pound of AI spend in this round.
options.insightRevenue: Well-matched customers activate faster, engage more deeply, and generate compounding value through every stage. The CVI advantage built at Acquisition carries all the way through to Loyalty.

compareSummary.reason: Lower AI cost than Option B with better targeting precision — the stronger revenue outcome reflects the quality difference in acquired customers, which compounds through every stage that follows.

options.explanation: This is the most effective approach: focus AI effort where conversion signals are strongest, and use simpler automation for the rest. By reserving full AI personalisation for the highest-potential prospects — where sector, growth stage, and digital engagement all point toward genuine readiness — the system acquires well-matched customers at the right cost. At £0.9M, it is the most cost-efficient acquisition option in the simulation. The CVI trajectory reflects this: better-matched customers activate faster, engage more deeply, and generate more lifetime value. Every stage that follows is more productive because the right customers entered the journey with the right expectations.

options.label: Keep the existing rules-based campaign system — no AI personalisation, standard static segmentation across all prospects.
options.insightExperience: No AI personalisation at this stage. The existing system uses fixed segments and cannot respond to real-time signals or sector-specific patterns. The customers acquired are weaker and less aligned with what the bank offers.
options.insightCostDrivers: Cost is minimal at £200K — no AI processing, no automation overhead. The saving is real, but the quality of customers entering the journey is structurally lower from the start.
options.insightRevenue: Weaker customers generate less engagement at every stage. CVI starts at a lower point and the disadvantage builds — the downstream revenue loss is far larger than the cost saved at acquisition.

compareSummary.reason: Saves £700K versus Option A but removes the AI targeting that separates strong prospects from weak ones — the result is a structurally weaker customer base that suppresses revenue at every stage that follows.

options.explanation: Without AI at acquisition, the bank relies on static segments that cannot respond to real-time signals or growth indicators. At £200K, costs are minimal — but the quality of customers entering the journey is structurally lower. The incoming customer base is weaker, less well-matched, and starts the journey without the advantage that AI-driven targeting creates. The CVI shortfall at this stage reflects that quality difference — and the revenue gap versus the Optimal AI Experience path reaches £1.5M by the end of Acquisition, far exceeding the cost saved.

rounds.title: How much should AI automate SME onboarding?
rounds.tradeoffTagline: 🤝 Trust formation vs ⚡ Speed and automation
rounds.prompt: The bank is designing how AI will guide new SME customers through onboarding — account setup, identity checks, and initial configuration. The key decision is how the AI operates: does it work automatically without explanation, guide customers step-by-step with human backup available, or leave the process manual?

options.label: Automate onboarding fully with AI — fast completion, but no explanation of decisions, no human backup, and no visibility into how the process works.
options.insightExperience: Onboarding is fast, but customers receive no explanation of how decisions are made and have no route to a human. At the moment SMEs form their first real impression of the bank, the experience feels controlled and opaque rather than transparent.
options.insightCostDrivers: The £1M cost covers AI processing across the full onboarding workflow plus automated document handling — comparable to the guided option, but without the transparency or human oversight that would justify the spend.
options.insightRevenue: Opaque automation creates a trust problem that compounds into lower adoption, weaker engagement, and lower lifetime value. The CVI drop after onboarding is visible in the chart and does not recover.

compareSummary.reason: Similar spend to Option B but without any transparency in a high-trust moment — the trust damage converts a £1M AI investment into a £1.2M revenue loss and a compounding disadvantage through every stage that follows.

options.explanation: Speed without transparency is the defining failure at this stage. The AI processes identity checks, makes eligibility assessments, and configures accounts at high speed — but never explains its reasoning or offers a route to human review. For an SME forming its first real impression of the bank, opaque automated decisions create a trust problem that does not recover. AI processing across the full onboarding workflow drives costs to £1M. The trust loss is immediately visible in the CVI chart as a steep decline through Activation. Because trust damaged at onboarding compounds into lower adoption at every subsequent stage, this is the highest-damage decision in the entire simulation.

options.label: Guide customers through onboarding with AI — explain each step clearly, route exceptions to a human reviewer, and keep the customer informed of what is happening and why.
options.insightExperience: The AI guides customers through each step, explains what it is doing, and escalates exceptions to a human reviewer. Transparency at the most formative stage of the relationship builds the trust that every stage that follows depends on.
options.insightCostDrivers: The £1.1M cost covers AI processing with clear explanations, human review for exceptions, and identity workflow management. The small premium over Option A funds the transparency that produces the trust advantage.
options.insightRevenue: Trust built at onboarding compounds through every stage that follows — higher adoption, deeper engagement, stronger retention. The CVI trajectory shows the steepest positive uplift in the simulation, and the effect carries all the way to Loyalty.

compareSummary.reason: At comparable spend to Option A, it delivers £4.7M more in revenue by turning onboarding into a trust-building moment — transparency and human oversight are the choices that compound through every stage that follows.

options.explanation: This is the right approach: the AI guides, explains, and escalates — rather than deciding silently. The system walks customers through each step, surfaces its reasoning, and routes exceptions to a human reviewer. At £1.1M — marginally more than Option A — it is categorically better in outcome. The CVI trajectory shows the steepest positive uplift in the simulation at this stage. Customers who experience a transparent, guided onboarding adopt more services, engage more deeply, and are significantly more resilient to competitive pressure at Retention and Loyalty. This is the highest-impact decision in the entire simulation.

options.label: Keep the existing manual onboarding process — digital forms only, no AI guidance, no adaptive support.
options.insightExperience: No AI guidance at this stage. Customers navigate static forms alone — with no support when they struggle and no adaptation to their situation. This is the weakest possible experience at the most important moment in the relationship.
options.insightCostDrivers: Cost is minimal at £150K — no AI processing, no human routing. The saving is real, but the absence of AI at the highest-leverage stage in the early relationship creates a gap that persists through every stage that follows.
options.insightRevenue: Customers with a poor onboarding experience activate fewer features, engage less deeply, and generate lower lifetime value. CVI grows slowly, and the revenue shortfall that builds from this stage is the largest false economy in the entire journey.

compareSummary.reason: Saves £950K versus Option B but removes all AI capability from the most formative stage — no adaptive support, no proactive guidance, and a structural experience gap that costs roughly £4.5M in foregone downstream revenue.

options.explanation: Keeping manual forms leaves customers to navigate onboarding alone. There is no guidance, no adaptation to where they are struggling, and the same static process regardless of the customer's profile or situation. At £150K, costs are minimal — but the experience gap is structural. SME customers who navigate a fragmented, unsupported onboarding are measurably less likely to activate key features, engage with advisory services, or expand their product usage. The drag shows up in the CVI chart from this stage forward and does not self-correct. The compounding disadvantage produces a £4.5M revenue shortfall against the Optimal AI Experience path by the end of the simulation.

rounds.title: How should AI guide customers through first use?
rounds.prompt: Newly onboarded SME customers need help getting started with their services. The bank is deciding how the AI should guide them through first use. The key trade-off is between guidance quality and AI cost: how intelligent and up-to-date should the AI's support be, and how much should the bank spend to deliver it?

options.label: Use AI to generate guidance and update it only when the customer's behaviour signals a real change — relevant support at the right moments, without running AI continuously.
options.insightExperience: The AI provides guidance based on what the customer is actually doing, updating when their behaviour changes meaningfully. Customers feel supported at the right moments — not overwhelmed by constant prompts — which builds trust rather than erodes it.
options.insightCostDrivers: The £700K cost covers AI at the moments that matter, plus lightweight signal monitoring — the system avoids running AI when nothing has changed. This produces the best revenue return per pound of AI spend in this round.
options.insightRevenue: Customers who activate well engage more deeply and respond more readily to expansion recommendations. The CVI uplift carries forward, and the revenue advantage compounds through Engagement and Expansion.

compareSummary.reason: Delivers stronger revenue at less than half the cost of Option B — relevant guidance at the right moments, without running the most powerful AI model continuously.

options.explanation: This is the most effective activation approach: generate useful guidance, keep it fresh, and update only when the customer's behaviour signals something has genuinely changed. The AI focuses its effort on moments that matter rather than running continuously. At £0.7M, this is the most cost-efficient option in this round. The guidance feels relevant and earned rather than intrusive, which builds trust. The CVI trajectory reflects this: a sustained uplift that carries into Engagement because customers who activate well engage more deeply. The best revenue return per pound of AI spend in the simulation at this stage.

options.label: Use the most powerful AI model to generate fresh guidance at every session — maximum quality at each interaction, running continuously regardless of whether anything has changed.
options.insightExperience: The AI applies maximum quality at every session, whether or not the customer's situation has changed. Guidance quality is high, but the system cannot distinguish between routine moments and genuinely new ones — applying the same level of effort to both.
options.insightCostDrivers: The £1.6M cost comes from running a high-end AI model at every session without any caching — more than double Option A. The premium pays for model quality, not for knowing when that quality is actually needed.
options.insightRevenue: The quality advantage over Option A does not produce proportionate revenue gain. The excess spend also reduces budget available for later stages, and the CVI advantage is small relative to the cost difference.

compareSummary.reason: Spends £0.9M more than Option A for a marginal quality improvement — running a high-end AI model at every session regardless of whether it is needed produces £1.3M less revenue than the more targeted alternative.

options.explanation: Running the highest-quality AI model at every session prioritises raw quality over good judgement — and the cost difference is not justified by the marginal improvement. At £1.6M, this costs more than double Option A. The core problem is that the system cannot tell when maximum AI effort is actually needed: it applies the same processing to a routine account check as to a genuinely complex situation. The CVI trajectory shows early strength but flattens as the budget drain limits investment at higher-leverage stages ahead. This is a technology-preference decision — maximum model quality — applied without cost discipline.

options.label: Give customers a static activation checklist — no AI guidance, no adaptive support based on how they are actually using the product.
options.insightExperience: No AI guidance at this stage. Customers navigate unfamiliar services alone — with no support when they struggle and no proactive help. This is the lowest-effort option at the stage with the highest first-impression leverage.
options.insightCostDrivers: Cost is minimal at £100K — no AI processing, no guidance system. The saving is real, but the behavioural gap created by unguided activation is structural and does not recover at later stages.
options.insightRevenue: Customers who activate poorly adopt fewer features and engage less. CVI growth stalls, and the depth of engagement needed to drive strong Expansion revenue is never fully established. The compounding revenue loss far exceeds the cost saved at this stage.

compareSummary.reason: Saves £600K versus Option A but removes all AI guidance at activation — customers who navigate alone activate slowly and never fully recover their engagement depth, costing £3.5M in foregone revenue.

options.explanation: A static checklist cannot adapt to where the customer is, what they have already tried, or where they are struggling. Without guidance, SME customers navigate unfamiliar services alone — activation is slower, incomplete, and leaves weaker engagement patterns. At £100K, the cost is minimal, but the gap is structural: customers who activate poorly generate lower engagement at Expansion and weaker resilience at Retention and Loyalty. The CVI shortfall at this stage is the direct consequence of removing AI at the moment when contextual guidance has the highest leverage in the early journey.

rounds.title: How much real-time AI intelligence should drive ongoing engagement?
rounds.prompt: SME customers are now actively using the bank. The bank is deciding how AI should support them day-to-day — covering cash flow alerts, business decision support, and proactive guidance. The key trade-off is how to allocate AI effort: apply it across every interaction, focus it on complex situations that genuinely need it, or limit it to periodic summaries.

options.label: Use AI to monitor every customer interaction in real time — continuous, always-on intelligence at every touchpoint, with no filtering or prioritisation of which interactions it covers.
options.insightExperience: The AI monitors every interaction — routine and complex — with the same intensity. Customers who sense constant AI observation become guarded rather than engaged. The experience starts to feel more like being watched than being supported.
options.insightCostDrivers: The £1.7M cost covers continuous AI monitoring across every touchpoint with no filtering — the most expensive engagement approach, buying volume of observation rather than quality of support.
options.insightRevenue: Engagement metrics improve in the short term, then reverse sharply. Trust erodes as customers feel constantly monitored, and CVI declines through Retention and Loyalty. The most expensive option in this round produces the worst long-term outcome.

compareSummary.reason: Short-term engagement is higher than Option C, but monitoring everything without filtering creates an experience that feels intrusive — trust erodes, the late-stage CVI reverses sharply, and it costs £800K more than the better-designed alternative.

options.explanation: Monitoring every interaction at the same intensity mistakes volume for value. The system processes routine cash flow alerts, standard transactions, and high-stakes decisions with identical AI effort — it cannot distinguish a moment that needs intelligence from one that does not. Real-time AI across all touchpoints drives costs to £1.7M, among the highest in the simulation. Trust begins to erode as customers sense they are being constantly monitored: the CVI trajectory shows early strength that reverses sharply at Retention and Loyalty. The short-term £1M revenue gain is more than offset by the relationship damage it creates downstream.

options.label: Use a smart routing model — handle routine interactions with simple rules, and apply AI only for complex situations, high-value moments, and genuine edge cases.
options.insightExperience: The AI focuses its effort on situations that genuinely need it — routine tasks handled simply, AI applied when complexity or high value warrants it. Customers receive support at the moments it matters most, which builds rather than erodes trust over time.
options.insightCostDrivers: The £900K cost covers selective AI processing plus the logic that classifies which interactions need it — the investment is in knowing when to apply AI, not in applying it everywhere.
options.insightRevenue: Customers who trust the AI engagement model use more services, engage more deeply, and are more receptive to expansion recommendations. CVI and cumulative revenue are the highest in this round, with the effect compounding through Expansion and Loyalty.

compareSummary.reason: Delivers four times the revenue of Option A at nearly half the cost — focusing AI on the interactions that genuinely need it, rather than monitoring everything, is the principle that separates this approach from the alternatives.

options.explanation: This is the most effective engagement model: apply simple rules to routine interactions, and reserve AI for complex situations, cash flow emergencies, and genuine moments of uncertainty. At £0.9M, this is the most cost-efficient engagement approach in the simulation. Customers receive AI support when it genuinely adds value — which feels helpful rather than intrusive — and trust is preserved and compounds. The CVI trajectory shows the strongest and most sustained uplift at this stage, carrying through Expansion and Loyalty. The principle embedded in this decision: AI leverage comes from focusing effort on the right moments, not from monitoring everything.

options.label: Use AI to generate periodic account summaries — batch processing only, no real-time support, no proactive engagement.
options.insightExperience: The AI produces periodic summaries — no real-time support, no awareness of emerging situations. The experience is retrospective: it describes what has already happened, but cannot help customers navigate what is happening now or what to do next.
options.insightCostDrivers: Cost is minimal at £150K — batch processing only, no real-time AI pipeline. The saving is real, but the absence of live intelligence at the engagement stage means customers are unsupported precisely when AI would have the most impact.
options.insightRevenue: Customers who are not proactively supported during active engagement disengage gradually. Feature adoption plateaus, receptiveness to expansion falls, and cumulative revenue falls significantly behind the Optimal AI Experience path.

compareSummary.reason: Saves £750K versus Option B but produces a reactive system at the highest-leverage stage of the journey — batch processing cannot respond to emerging cash flow risk or surface expansion opportunities in time, costing £5.5M in foregone revenue.

options.explanation: Periodic summaries create a reactive experience at the stage where AI adds the most value. Without real-time intelligence, the system cannot respond to emerging cash flow problems, flag expansion opportunities when the customer is ready, or support decisions as they arise — it only reports on what has already happened. Batch processing keeps costs minimal at £150K, but the timing gap is commercially decisive. SME customers who receive no proactive support during active engagement disengage measurably by Expansion. The £1.5M revenue loss at this stage understates the cumulative impact — the absence of live intelligence at the highest-leverage stage creates a declining trajectory that compounds through Retention and Loyalty.

rounds.title: What should power AI-enabled growth recommendations?
rounds.prompt: Active SME customers are ready to expand — credit, additional products, adjacent services. The bank is designing the AI system that will identify and surface these opportunities. The key decision is how that system is built: a custom-trained model optimised for the bank's commercial priorities, a real-time system grounded in live customer signals, or the existing rules-based engine.

options.label: Build a custom AI model trained on the bank's SME transaction history — proprietary, high cost to build and maintain, with the bank's commercial priorities built into how it makes recommendations.
options.insightExperience: The AI recommends using a model trained around what the bank wants to sell, not what the customer needs to grow. Recommendations appear personalised but are systematically oriented toward bank revenue targets. Sophisticated SME customers at this stage detect the misalignment.
options.insightCostDrivers: The £1.9M cost covers model training, fine-tuning on proprietary data, and ongoing maintenance — the highest spend in this round. Most of the cost funds building the model, not the quality of experience it delivers.
options.insightRevenue: Initial conversion is reasonable, but trust erodes as the commercial bias becomes apparent. Receptiveness to future recommendations falls, and expansion revenue weakens in later stages. Revenue is £2.5M against the optimal path's £5M.

compareSummary.reason: Costs £700K more than Option C and builds commercial bias into how the AI recommends — customers detect the misalignment, trust weakens, and the late-stage trajectory deteriorates.

options.explanation: A custom-trained model creates a structural conflict: the AI is optimised for what the bank wants to sell, not what the customer needs to grow. Recommendations appear personalised but are systematically oriented toward bank revenue targets. At £1.9M — the highest spend in this round — most of the cost funds model building, not experience quality. The CVI shows initial strength as the recommendations feel relevant, but trust begins eroding as customers recognise the commercial orientation. Receptiveness to future recommendations falls, and the late-stage trajectory deteriorates. Revenue is £2.5M against the Optimal AI Experience path's £5M — the cost premium does not produce proportionate return.

options.label: Keep the existing rules-based recommendation engine — fixed product triggers, static customer segments, no AI inference or real-time adaptation.
options.insightExperience: No AI for expansion recommendations. The rules-based engine applies fixed product triggers to static customer segments — it cannot read the customer's current cash flow, growth trajectory, or genuine readiness to expand at any given moment.
options.insightCostDrivers: Cost is minimal at £200K — no AI processing, no real-time data access. The saving is real, but the static logic systematically misses the moment when a customer is actually ready to expand.
options.insightRevenue: Customers who receive poorly timed or irrelevant recommendations disengage from the recommendations layer entirely. CVI growth stalls, product adoption falls, and cumulative revenue falls materially short of the optimal path.

compareSummary.reason: Saves £1M versus Option C but applies static logic to a dynamic opportunity — the rules-based engine cannot read real-time customer signals, so it systematically misses the moment when customers are genuinely ready to expand.

options.explanation: A rules-based engine cannot read the signals needed for effective expansion targeting. It applies fixed product triggers to static customer segments — it cannot process cash flow trajectories, sector growth indicators, or real-time patterns that indicate when a customer is ready to expand. At £200K, costs are minimal, but expansion opportunities are systematically missed — the right product is offered at the wrong moment to the wrong customer. The CVI shortfall reflects those missed opportunities: customers who receive irrelevant or poorly timed recommendations disengage from the recommendations layer, and that disengagement compounds into lower retention and loyalty.

options.label: Use an AI system that retrieves live customer signals to ground recommendations in real context — relevant, data-grounded suggestions without the cost or commercial bias of a custom-trained model.
options.insightExperience: The AI pulls live signals — cash flow patterns, sector benchmarks, business cycle indicators — and builds recommendations around the customer's actual situation. Recommendations feel specific and earned, and appear to serve the customer's growth rather than the bank's sales targets.
options.insightCostDrivers: The £1.2M cost covers AI processing plus the retrieval layer that makes recommendations contextually accurate — £700K less than the custom-trained model, with better results.
options.insightRevenue: Contextually accurate, trust-aligned recommendations convert at significantly higher rates. CVI shows the largest single-stage uplift in the simulation, and the trust and adoption gains carry forward through Retention and Loyalty.

compareSummary.reason: Delivers twice the revenue of Option A at £700K less cost — recommendations grounded in live customer signals achieve better relevance and trust alignment than a custom-trained model, without the commercial bias.

options.explanation: This is the most effective expansion approach: an AI system that retrieves live customer signals — cash flow patterns, sector benchmarks, business cycle indicators — and grounds recommendations in the customer's actual situation rather than a commercial training objective. At £1.2M, it costs substantially less than Option A while delivering better results. The CVI trajectory shows the largest single-stage uplift in the simulation: recommendations that feel specific and earned convert at high rates. Trust is reinforced because the system appears to serve the customer's growth, not the bank's sales targets. This is the highest-return decision in the simulation.

rounds.title: How should AI intervene when SME customers show risk signals?
rounds.prompt: Early signals — falling transaction volume, reduced feature usage, increased support contacts — suggest some SME customers may be at risk of disengaging or facing financial difficulty. The bank is designing how AI will respond. The key decision is how the AI acts: autonomously without informing the customer, with human approval and transparent communication, or not at all until the customer raises a concern.

options.label: Allow AI to act autonomously on risk signals — no human approval required, and no explanation given to the customer of what triggered the intervention.
options.insightExperience: The AI acts on risk signals without asking for approval and without explaining what triggered the response. SME customers — potentially under financial pressure — receive interventions they did not request and cannot understand, at their most vulnerable moment in the relationship.
options.insightCostDrivers: The £1.4M cost covers continuous risk monitoring, signal classification, and automated intervention — the most expensive retention approach, spending on autonomous action with no oversight or transparency built in.
options.insightRevenue: Retention metrics improve in the short term, then reverse sharply. Trust destroyed by unexplained autonomous action creates a Loyalty-stage collapse that more than offsets the retention gain. Net revenue is lower than the transparent alternative despite higher spend.

compareSummary.reason: Retention metrics improve in the short term, but acting without explanation in a financially sensitive context destroys trust — the CVI reverses sharply at Loyalty as the relationship damage becomes apparent.

options.explanation: Acting without explanation is the core failure mode of AI in high-stakes financial situations. The system detects risk signals and acts unilaterally — no human oversight, no customer consent, no explanation of what triggered the response. At a stage when SME customers may be under genuine financial pressure, autonomous action — even well-intentioned — feels intrusive and opaque. Continuous risk monitoring and automated intervention drives costs to £1.4M. The CVI shows short-term retention metrics improve, then reverses sharply: trust destroyed by unexplained autonomous action creates a Loyalty-stage collapse that more than offsets the early retention gain. The intervention kept customers temporarily but destroyed the relationship quality that makes retention economically valuable.

options.label: Use AI to detect risk early, require human approval before acting, and tell the customer what has been flagged and why — keeping them informed throughout.
options.insightExperience: The AI detects risk signals and presents them to a human reviewer before any action is taken. The customer is then told what was flagged and why. This transparency turns a potential trust risk into a trust-building event — customers feel supported, not processed.
options.insightCostDrivers: The £1M cost covers risk detection, signal classification, and the human review workflow — the human approval step adds cost, but that oversight is what produces five times the revenue of Option A.
options.insightRevenue: Customers who receive transparent, human-approved support experience increased trust rather than erosion. CVI strengthens through Loyalty, retained customers generate materially higher lifetime value, and cumulative revenue is the strongest in this round.

compareSummary.reason: At £400K less than Option A, it delivers five times the revenue — the human approval step converts the intervention from a trust risk into a trust-building event, and that difference drives the entire outcome gap.

options.explanation: This is the right model for AI intervention at a high-stakes stage: detect risk signals early, require human approval before acting, and keep the customer informed throughout. At £1M, it is the most cost-efficient retention approach in this round. Customers who receive transparent, timely, human-approved support experience an increase in trust rather than a reduction — the CVI trajectory shows the strongest uplift in the simulation at this stage. The principle is straightforward: a retained SME customer who understands why the bank acted — and agreed to it — has measurably higher lifetime value than one retained through unexplained intervention.

options.label: Take no proactive action — wait for the customer to raise a concern or show clear signs of leaving before responding.
options.insightExperience: No proactive intervention. The bank responds only after the customer escalates — by which point disengagement is already entrenched. Customers experiencing early financial difficulty receive no support at the point when it would have the most impact.
options.insightCostDrivers: Cost is minimal at £100K — no risk detection, no AI processing, no intervention workflow. The saving is real, but the absence of early detection means the optimal window for effective action is missed entirely.
options.insightRevenue: By the time visible churn signals appear, CVI has already declined and the revenue loss is locked in. Acting early consistently outperforms late recovery — the £2M shortfall is the direct consequence of the timing gap.

compareSummary.reason: Saves £900K versus Option C but removes all proactive intelligence from the retention layer — by the time a customer raises a concern, the intervention window has already closed, and the £2M revenue loss reflects the cost of that timing failure.

options.explanation: Waiting means the intervention arrives after the window for effective action has already closed. Without early risk detection, the system cannot identify the behavioural signals that precede visible churn — falling transaction frequency, shifts in cash flow usage, reduced feature engagement. By the time a customer raises a concern directly, disengagement has become entrenched and recovery is materially more expensive. At £100K, AI costs are minimal, but the timing gap is commercially decisive: early intervention at low cost consistently outperforms late recovery at high cost. The £2M revenue loss reflects the value of the missed intervention window — and the CVI decline is the compounding consequence of not supporting the relationship when it had the most leverage.

rounds.title: How should AI shape the long-term SME banking relationship?
rounds.tradeoffTagline: 🌱 Long-term relationship value vs 💵 Short-term revenue extraction
rounds.prompt: The SME relationship is established. The bank is now deciding how AI will shape the customer's long-term experience — always-on intelligence that surfaces insights, anticipates needs, and positions the bank as a genuine business partner. The key decision is what the AI is optimised for: the customer's financial success, the bank's short-term revenue targets, or a templated approximation of personalisation.

options.label: Orient the AI around bank revenue extraction — upsell triggers, cross-sell prompts, and fee-generating actions prioritised by the model's commercial objective.
options.insightExperience: The AI optimises for bank revenue metrics — upsell rates, cross-sell conversion, fee triggers — rather than customer outcomes. SME customers who have experienced genuinely helpful AI across prior stages detect this shift and interpret it as a change in the bank's stance toward them.
options.insightCostDrivers: The £1M cost covers AI processing focused on commercial triggers — targeting the bank's revenue priorities rather than the customer's financial health. The spend builds extraction capability, not an advisory partnership.
options.insightRevenue: Short-term revenue increases, but trust erodes as the commercial orientation becomes apparent. Advocacy collapses, churn risk rises, and the long-term relationship value destroyed far exceeds the short-term gain.

compareSummary.reason: Generates more short-term revenue than Option C, but customers recognise AI designed around extraction — trust collapses, and the long-term relationship value destroyed far exceeds the short-term gain.

options.explanation: Optimising AI for commercial extraction builds misaligned incentives directly into the system. The AI learns to maximise bank-side metrics — upsell rates, cross-sell conversion, fee revenue — rather than customer financial health. At £1M, the cost covers commercial trigger processing rather than genuine advisory capability. SME customers at the Loyalty stage have enough experience with AI-enabled banking to distinguish recommendations that serve their interests from those that serve the bank's. When that distinction becomes apparent — which it does quickly — trust erodes, advocacy collapses, and customers begin evaluating alternatives. The CVI reflects this: a short-term revenue increase that reverses into structural long-term value destruction that compounds for as long as the relationship continues.

options.label: Orient the AI around the SME's financial success — insights, support, and recommendations designed to help the customer's business grow, with bank revenue as the downstream consequence of a genuine partnership.
